definition: to make a serious, formal promise, often by taking an oath.

collocations.example: New citizens must swear an oath of loyalty.
Witnesses swear to tell the truth in court.

definition: to clean a floor or surface by brushing away dust and dirt.

collocations.example: She swept the floor after the party ended.
Please sweep up the broken glass carefully.

definition: a swinging movement of the arm or a club when hitting a ball.

collocations.example: He practices his golf swing every weekend.
The batter took a wild swing and missed.

definition: a small device that you press to turn electrical equipment on or off.

collocations.example: The light switch is next to the door.
Press the power switch to start the machine.

definition: a weapon with a long sharp metal blade and a handle.

collocations.example: The knight drew his sword before the battle.
The soldier carried a sword and shield.

definition: a story about imaginary events or people, often exciting.

collocations.example: The children love hearing a fairy tale at bedtime.
This folk tale has been passed down for generations.

definition: a large container for holding liquid or gas.

collocations.example: The water tank on the roof was empty.
They filled the fuel tank before the long trip.

definition: a device that controls the flow of water from a pipe.

collocations.example: Is the tap water safe to drink here?
Please turn off the tap to save water.

definition: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.

collocations.example: We decided to take a taxi to the airport.
The taxi driver knew the fastest route downtown.

definition: to laugh at or make fun of someone in a playful way.

collocations.example: She would tease him gently about his cooking.
They always tease him about his funny accent.

definition: scientific knowledge used to make machines, tools, and systems.

collocations.example: Modern technology has changed how we communicate daily.
She works in the information technology department.

definition: relating to a person who is between thirteen and nineteen years old.

collocations.example: The teenage girl spends hours on her phone.
Their teenage son just started high school.

definition: to make someone want to do or have something, often something unwise.

collocations.example: Low prices tempt customers to buy more items.
The warm weather tempted us to skip work.

definition: nervous or worried, and unable to relax.

collocations.example: There was a tense atmosphere in the meeting room.
Everyone felt nervous during the tense situation.

definition: a shelter made of cloth that you use when camping.

collocations.example: We decided to pitch a tent near the lake.
They bought a new camping tent for the trip.

definition: a building where plays and other performances take place.

collocations.example: We often go to the theater on weekends.
The new movie theater has twelve large screens.

definition: for that reason; as a result of something.

collocations.example: He was late and therefore missed the opening speech.
The budget is tight; we therefore must cut costs.

definition: a person who steals something from another person or place.

collocations.example: The police managed to catch the thief quickly.
A car thief broke into the parking lot.

definition: having a small distance between two opposite sides; not thick.

collocations.example: Spread a thin layer of butter on the bread.
She cut a thin slice of cheese for me.

definition: something or someone that could cause harm or danger.

collocations.example: Pollution can pose a threat to public health.
The airport treated the package as a security threat.

definition: as a result of what has just been said; therefore.

collocations.example: The project has gone smoothly thus far.
She trained hard and thus won the race.

definition: a printed piece of paper that shows you have paid to travel or enter.

collocations.example: I bought a train ticket to the city.
The ticket price includes a free museum tour.

definition: the regular rise and fall of the sea's level during the day.

collocations.example: The beach disappears completely at high tide.
We collected shells on the sand at low tide.

definition: a soft silver-white metal often used to coat other metals.

collocations.example: The miners extracted tin ore from the hills.
Bronze is made from copper and tin.

definition: extremely small in size or amount.

collocations.example: Add only a tiny amount of salt.
They spent a week on a tiny island.

definition: a small amount of money you give to someone for their service.

collocations.example: We always leave a tip for good service.
She gave the waiter a generous tip tonight.

definition: the name given to a book, film, or piece of work.

collocations.example: I forgot the book title but remember the author.
The author's name appears on the title page.

definition: slices of bread that have been made brown by heating.

collocations.example: She ate buttered toast with her morning coffee.
He had a piece of toast for breakfast.

definition: one of the five separate parts at the end of your foot.

collocations.example: He broke his big toe playing football.
I stubbed my toe on the bed frame.

definition: a large bowl that you use to get rid of waste from your body.

collocations.example: Remember to flush the toilet after using it.
The public toilet near the station was clean.

definition: a soft red fruit eaten raw or cooked as a vegetable.

collocations.example: She added tomato sauce to the pasta dish.
He put a cherry tomato in the salad.

definition: the quality of someone's voice that shows how they feel.

collocations.example: Her tone of voice showed real concern.
He answered the question in an angry tone.

definition: the soft part inside your mouth that you use for tasting and speaking.

collocations.example: The child stuck out her tongue at me.
Be careful not to burn your tongue on the soup.

definition: a piece of equipment you hold in your hand to do a job.

collocations.example: He bought a new power tool for the workshop.
A hammer is a common hand tool.

definition: a subject that people talk, write, or learn about.

collocations.example: Climate change is a hot topic these days.
Her speech became the main topic of discussion.

definition: difficult to do or to deal with.

collocations.example: Choosing between the two offers was a tough decision.
Repairing the old roof was a tough job.

definition: a journey in which you visit several places in an area.

collocations.example: We took a guided tour of the castle.
The city tour lasted about three hours.

definition: a piece of cloth used for drying your body or things.

collocations.example: She wrapped herself in a warm bath towel.
He wiped the spill with a paper towel.

definition: a tall narrow structure or part of a building.

collocations.example: The clock tower chimes every hour on time.
The pilot contacted the control tower before landing.

definition: an object for a child to play with.

collocations.example: The boy pushed his toy car across the floor.
We bought a gift at the toy store.

definition: a very small amount or sign that something exists or happened.

collocations.example: There was a trace of sadness in her smile.
The ship vanished without a trace at sea.

definition: the activity of buying and selling goods or services.

collocations.example: Foreign trade is important for the country's economy.
The two nations signed a free trade agreement.

definition: a custom or belief passed from one generation to the next.

collocations.example: Giving gifts is an old cultural tradition here.
Baking cookies at Christmas is a family tradition.

definition: the vehicles moving along roads in a particular area.

collocations.example: We were stuck in heavy traffic for hours.
A traffic jam delayed our arrival this morning.

definition: to move someone or something from one place to another.

collocations.example: You can transfer money between accounts online.
We need to transfer data to the new server.

definition: a device for catching animals, often hidden from view.

collocations.example: They set a trap to catch the mice.
The fox was caught in a metal trap.

definition: a flat object with raised edges used for carrying things.

collocations.example: She placed the cookies on a baking tray.
The waiter carried a tray of drinks carefully.

definition: a legal process where a court decides if someone is guilty.

collocations.example: He will stand trial for the robbery next month.
Every person deserves a fair trial in court.

definition: something you do to deceive or fool someone.

collocations.example: The children played a trick on their teacher.
He used a clever trick to fool his friends.

definition: a large road vehicle used for carrying heavy goods.

collocations.example: The truck driver delivered the goods on time.
He loaded the furniture into his pickup truck.

definition: the thick main stem of a tree from which branches grow.

collocations.example: A squirrel ran up the tall tree trunk.
An owl nested inside the hollow trunk.

definition: a series of musical notes that are pleasant to listen to.

collocations.example: The advert has a very catchy tune.
She began to hum a tune while cooking.

definition: one of two children born to the same mother at the same time.

collocations.example: His twin brother looks exactly like him.
The identical twins confused all their teachers.

definition: to turn something using your hand, especially to open it.

collocations.example: She had to twist the lid hard to open it.
You can twist off the cap easily.

definition: having the usual qualities of a particular type of thing.

collocations.example: This painting is typical of his early work.
This building is a typical example of modern design.

definition: an organization of workers formed to protect their rights.

collocations.example: The trade union negotiated higher wages for members.
Many employees decided to join a union.

definition: a single thing that is complete in itself but part of something larger.

collocations.example: The control unit manages the entire system.
Each business unit reports its own profits.

definition: to join together with others to achieve a common goal.

collocations.example: The villagers united against the new tax.
Small firms often unite with larger partners.

definition: a place where students study for a degree after secondary school.

collocations.example: The university student studied late in the library.
She earned a university degree in economics.

definition: located above or higher than something else.

collocations.example: Their apartment is on the upper floor.
The upper limit for the loan is fixed.

definition: feeling unhappy or worried because something bad has happened.

collocations.example: She tends to get upset over small problems.
He was visibly upset after the bad news.

definition: a low area of land between hills or mountains.

collocations.example: The river valley is rich with green farmland.
Snow covered the quiet mountain valley all winter.

definition: the amount of money that something is worth.

collocations.example: The market value of the house has risen.
The painting is of great value to collectors.

definition: several different; of many different kinds.

collocations.example: There are various ways to solve this problem.
He was absent for various reasons last week.

definition: to be different in size, amount, or degree from each other.

collocations.example: The apples vary in size and color.
Prices vary from one shop to another.

definition: a plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot.

collocations.example: Spinach is a healthy green vegetable to eat.
She made a warm vegetable soup for lunch.

definition: a machine such as a car or truck used for transporting people or goods.

collocations.example: You need a license to drive a motor vehicle.
The company bought a new commercial vehicle for deliveries.

definition: a form of something that is slightly different from other forms.

collocations.example: Please download the latest version of the app.
I prefer the original version of the song.

definition: a person who has been harmed or hurt by someone or something.

collocations.example: Many tourists fall victim to petty theft.
He was a victim of a cruel scam.

definition: a small group of houses and buildings in the countryside.

collocations.example: She grew up in a small village in Wales.
The old fishing village attracts many summer tourists.

definition: using physical force intended to hurt or kill someone.

collocations.example: Violent crime has decreased in the city recently.
The club bans any kind of violent behavior.

definition: a formal choice that you make in an election or meeting.

collocations.example: Every citizen can cast a vote in the election.
Most members voted for the new proposal.

definition: the money you are paid regularly for the work you do.

collocations.example: Many workers earn only the minimum wage.
Her hourly wage increased after the promotion.

definition: to walk around slowly in no particular direction.

collocations.example: We liked to wander around the old town.
The child began to wander off from the group.

definition: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem.

collocations.example: Signs warn of falling rocks on the road.
Doctors warn against eating too much sugar.

definition: not having much physical strength or power.

collocations.example: She was too weak to lift the box.
His weak legs trembled after the long climb.

definition: an object such as a gun or knife used to hurt people.

collocations.example: The treaty aims to reduce nuclear weapon stockpiles.
A loaded gun is clearly a lethal weapon.

definition: to marry someone.

collocations.example: The young couple plan to wed next spring.
They chose to wed in a small church.

definition: a wild plant that grows where it is not wanted.

collocations.example: He sprayed weed killer along the garden path.
She spent the morning pulling up weeds.

definition: very strange or unusual, often in a way that is hard to explain.

collocations.example: I had a weird feeling someone was watching.
His new haircut looks really weird to me.

definition: a greeting or reception given to someone when they arrive.

collocations.example: The host gave us a warm welcome.
The visiting singer was given a royal welcome.

definition: located in or coming from the west part of a place.

collocations.example: Heavy rain hit the western region of the state.
They sailed along the western coast of the island.

definition: used to compare or contrast two different facts.

collocations.example: Some people love winter, whereas others hate it.
Now she drives, whereas before she always walked.

definition: a long thin piece of leather used to hit animals or people.

collocations.example: The rider cracked the whip and the horse ran.
He carried a long leather whip on his belt.

definition: a small device that makes a high sound when you blow into it.

collocations.example: The referee blew the whistle to stop play.
He gave a loud whistle to call the dog.

definition: morally very bad; evil.

collocations.example: The villain was punished for his wicked deeds.
The wicked witch cast a spell on the prince.

definition: one of the parts of a bird, insect, or plane used for flying.

collocations.example: The eagle spread its wings and flew away.
Ice formed on the aircraft wing during the flight.

definition: to clean or dry something by rubbing it with a cloth.

collocations.example: Please wipe the table before we eat.
He wiped the dust off the old shelf.

definition: a thin thread of metal used for carrying electricity or fastening things.

collocations.example: The electrician connected the copper wire carefully.
A barbed wire fence surrounded the field.

definition: able to make good decisions based on knowledge and experience.

collocations.example: Buying the house was a wise decision.
The wise old man gave the children advice.

definition: a person who sees an event or gives evidence in a court of law.

collocations.example: An expert witness explained the medical evidence clearly.
The lawyer decided to call a witness.

definition: a wild animal of the dog family that hunts in groups.

collocations.example: A gray wolf appeared at the forest edge.
A pack of wolves howled through the night.

definition: the soft thick hair of sheep, used to make cloth and yarn.

collocations.example: This blanket is made from pure wool.
She knitted a warm wool sweater for winter.

definition: a small long thin creature with no bones or legs that lives in soil.

collocations.example: The birds dig up worms after the rain.
She found a slimy worm under the rock.

definition: an injury to the body, especially one where the skin is cut.

collocations.example: The nurse cleaned the open wound carefully.
It took weeks for the wound to heal.

definition: to cover something by folding paper or cloth around it.

collocations.example: She likes to wrap each gift with care.
He wrapped a scarf around his neck.

definition: to shout something very loudly, often in anger or excitement.

collocations.example: Don't yell at the children like that.
He yelled out a warning to the driver.

definition: pieces of material made of crossed threads with holes, used to catch fish.

collocations.example: The sailors pulled in their heavy fishing nets.
At dawn they cast the nets into the sea.

definition: relating to the differences between groups of people based on race.

collocations.example: The law forbids racial discrimination in hiring.
They marched peacefully to demand racial equality.
